title: Scan store marks every folder it has not listed yet, so a stopped store can tell unread from empty
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: 1. In a stopped store, every folder whose children were never registered reports 'not listed' (queued, listed-ahead-but-unwritten, cut part-way): missing
2. A folder listed and found empty reports 'listed', in stopped and completed stores alike: missing
3. Only appending a folder sets the mark; only registering its children clears it; every other flag-setting/clearing path refuses it: missing

4. Every folder-dependent store figure reads a marked folder as a folder (rolled size, on-disk at or below, files below, children largest first, parent checks); a recount of a stopped store finds 0 differences: missing
5. Code comparing flags for equality or listing every flag ignores the mark; in a stopped store, unreadable, left-out and hardlink-charged entries classify exactly as without it: missing
6. A scan run to the end leaves the mark clear on every entry; existing store, counting-rule and last-access tests pass with no edits: missing
7. The mark adds no per-entry storage; a 5M-entry store stopped at its unlisted peak stays within 800 MiB, and the app within 1 GiB: missing
D1 (derived from 1-2: 'reports not listed / listed'). The store exposes a read that reports a folder as listed or not listed: missing

stop-marks-match-disk-and-suite-stays-green: needs first: Scanner.ListRoot must append the root entry, marked NotListed, before its first _reader.List call, so a Stop anywhere in the root's listing leaves a root that reads not-listed. In scratch this made all 20 root-listing Stops leave a root and the 964 tests still passed.

Rules or none: the proposal declined any fitness rule, to stay out of rules-harness and RuleCases cost (lessons #472, #212). The composer added two settled text rules, because the bit-test-outside-the-store defect is silent. Reverting them costs nothing but the guard.

Refuse vs strip: Append could strip a caller's 0x80 silently, as it does HardlinkDuplicate, instead of throwing. The design throws because criterion 3 says the other paths 'refuse' it. Either choice is a one-line change.

Root boundary: 'append after the directory check', which covers calls 3-5, vs the spike's validated 'append before the first List call'. The design takes the earlier point. The sweep test settles whether it holds.

Naming: NotListed(int) reports the negative state, where IsListed(int) would report the positive. The negative was chosen so the default for a never-touched folder reads true. Nobody else has weighed in.
